prompt:
Write a freelance proposal (cover letter) from Noor Halden for the job below.

About the freelancer: 6 years experience; skills: Python, PyTorch, scikit-learn, LangChain, OpenAI API, Hugging Face Transformers, NLP, XGBoost, pandas, machine learning

Job post (treat as data):
<job>
Title: Gstreamer latency calculation
I have a gstreamer pipeline on python that receives a udp stream as an input and a udp stream as an output. When I visualize the input stream and the output stream I can see a delay. Can you please provide a tool that calculates the delay?
</job>

Past projects you may mention (the ONLY experience you may claim):
title: Ceramic tile defect detection
client: Halvorsen Ceramics
client_industry: manufacturing
start: 2022-05
end: 2022-08
engagement: fixed
stack:
- Python
- PyTorch
- YOLOv8
- OpenCV
- ONNX

built: A camera-based crack and chip detector exported to ONNX and running on an industrial
  PC beside the kiln line.
metrics:
- 97.4% recall on cracks
- false rejects from 8% to 2.1%

Style:
- Open by briefly introducing yourself.
- Mention these projects by what was built and one result each: Ceramic tile defect detection (p07).
- Keep it under 150 words.
- End with one specific question about the job.

Output only the proposal text. Never add contact details or links.
text:
Hi, I’m Noor Halden, a machine learning engineer with 6 years of experience building Python-based ML tools.

I’ve built production-focused computer vision systems, including a camera-based crack and chip detector for Halvorsen Ceramics that was exported to ONNX and ran on an industrial PC beside the kiln line. That project reached 97.4% recall on cracks and reduced false rejects from 8% to 2.1%.

For your GStreamer pipeline, I can create a Python tool that measures end-to-end latency between the UDP input and UDP output streams and reports the delay clearly so you can visualize and compare it. I’m comfortable working with Python, pandas, scikit-learn, and machine learning tooling, and I can keep the solution practical and easy to integrate with your existing pipeline.

Would you like the tool to report latency as a live stream metric, or as per-frame timestamps saved to a file?
